metadata.methods_description: Simultaneous EEG-fMRI was acquired with a 64-channel MR-compatible Brain Products system (5 kHz sampling) and a 3T Siemens Verio scanner (EPI, TR=1 s, TE=23 ms, 2x2x4 mm, 16 slices). Each session had five runs with a 20 s rest/20 s task block design: motor imagery pre-test, three neurofeedback runs, and motor imagery post-test. EEG was preprocessed in BrainVision Analyzer with gradient and ballistocardiogram artifact correction, downsampling to 200 Hz, and a 50 Hz low-pass filter.

citation_details.abstract: This paper reports on a benchmark dataset acquired with a brain-computer interface (BCI) system based on the rapid serial visual presentation (RSVP) paradigm. The dataset consists of 64-channel electroencephalogram (EEG) data from 64 healthy subjects (sub1,…, sub64) while they performed a target image detection task. For each subject, the data contained two groups ("A" and "B"). Each group contained two blocks, and each block included 40 trials that corresponded to 40 stimulus sequences. Each sequence contained 100 images presented at 10 Hz (10 images per second). The stimulus images were street-view images of two categories: target images with human and non-target images without human. Target images were presented randomly in the stimulus sequence with a probability of 1∼4%. These measures are usually acquired from a single modality, most commonly electroencephalography (EEG) or functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). EEG-fMRI-neurofeedback (EEG-fMRI-NF) is a new approach that consists in providing a NF based simultaneously on EEG and fMRI signals. citation_details.title: Impact of 1D and 2D Visualisation on EEG-fMRI Neurofeedback Training During a Motor Imagery Task
citation_details.author: Claire Cury, Giulia Lioi, Lorraine Perronnet, Anatole Lécuyer, Pierre Maurel, Christian Barillot
citation_details.venue: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
citation_details.abstract: Bi-modal EEG-fMRI neurofeedback (NF) is a new technique of great interest. First, it can improve the quality of NF training by combining different real-time information (haemody-namic and electrophysiological) from the participant's brain activity; Second, it has potential to better understand the link and the synergy between the two modalities (EEG-fMRI). However there are different ways to show to the participant his NF scores during bi-modal NF sessions. To improve data fusion methodologies, we investigate the impact of a 1D or 2D representation when a visual feedback is given during motor imagery task. Results show a better synergy between EEG and fMRI when a 2D display is used. Subjects have better fMRI scores when 1D is used for bi-modal EEG-fMRI NF sessions; on the other hand, they regulate EEG more specifically when the 2D metaphor is used.
